name: Sarah Waters
knownFor: Novelist of lesbian love in Victorian and wartime England: Tipping the Velvet and Fingersmith.
bio: Sarah Waters was born in Neyland, Pembrokeshire, and grew up in Middlesbrough. She studied English literature, taking a BA at the University of Kent, an MA at Lancaster and a PhD at Queen Mary, University of London, and went from her doctoral thesis on gay and lesbian historical fiction directly to her first novel.

Her novels are best known for their Victorian settings and lesbian heroines. All but one of her books have lesbian themes, and she does not mind being labelled a lesbian writer: she has said she writes "with a clear lesbian agenda". Her fiction mixes the sensation novel, the historical novel and the ghost story.

works.title: Tipping the Velvet
works.note: her debut, a music-hall romance; won a Betty Trask Award; a BBC mini-series in 2002

works.title: Affinity
works.note: set among Victorian Spiritualists; won the Stonewall Book Award and the Somerset Maugham Award

works.title: Fingersmith
works.note: shortlisted for the Booker Prize and the Orange Prize; filmed in Korea as The Handmaiden (2016)

works.title: The Little Stranger
works.note: a ghost story; her first novel with no overtly lesbian characters

events.text: Published her first novel, Tipping the Velvet.
Won a Betty Trask Award for Tipping the Velvet, and published Affinity.
Fingersmith was published and shortlisted for the Booker and Orange prizes; the BBC filmed Tipping the Velvet the same year.
The BBC broadcast a three-part adaptation of Fingersmith.
Published The Little Stranger, a postwar ghost story.
Park Chan-wook's film The Handmaiden, adapted from Fingersmith and set in Korea, was released.

relevance: Waters writes the lesbian novel as high-end historical fiction: plotting, period detail and sensation in the Wilkie Collins tradition, with women's desire at the centre of it. Her work shows how far the genre can range beyond the contemporary romance.
influence: Her novels were adapted for the BBC and, in Fingersmith's case, for Korean cinema, and she has done much to put lesbian historical fiction in the mainstream.
